record.paper_title: Problems in Data Structures and Algorithms
record.original_question: Let w1, w2, ..., wn be positive weights on n ordered items, and consider alphabetic binary search trees in which the items may appear only in the external nodes (leaves), with the i-th external node at depth di in symmetric order. What is the true complexity of constructing a tree minimizing Σ_i w_i d_i? In particular, can this problem be solved in linear time, or can one prove a lower bound ruling that out?

evidence.quote: Problem 6.2 Items can be stored only in the external nodes (the leaves) of the tree. The problem in this case is: Given positive weights w1, w2,...,wn, construct a binary tree with n external nodes that minimizes n i=1 widi , where di is the depth of the i-th external node in symmetric order.

And again, there is no lower bound known. In fact, there is no reason to believe that the problem cannot be solved in linear time, and there is good reason to believe that maybe it can: for some interesting special cases the problem can indeed be solved in linear time [27].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n\ge 1$ and let $w_1,w_2,\dots,w_n$ be positive real weights associated with $n$ items given in a fixed linear order. An *alphabetic binary tree* for these items is a rooted binary tree with exactly $n$ external nodes (leaves) such that, when the leaves are listed in symmetric (left-to-right) order, the $i$-th leaf corresponds to the $i$-th item. For such a tree let $d_i$ denote the depth (number of edges from the root) of the leaf carrying the $i$-th item. The *cost* of the tree is
$$C = \sum_{i=1}^{n} w_i\, d_i,$$
and an alphabetic binary tree minimizing $C$ is called optimal.

Determine the true time complexity, in the comparison-based model on a real-RAM with the weights as input, of constructing an optimal alphabetic binary tree. In particular, decide whether there exists an algorithm running in time $O(n)$ for arbitrary positive real weights, or prove a super-linear lower bound that rules this out.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is solvable in O(n log n) time by the Hu–Tucker (and Garsia–Wachs) algorithm, and linear-time algorithms are known for special cases (e.g., when weights come from a domain sortable in linear time, or for certain structured input classes; an O(n sqrt(log n)) bound exists for integer instances). However, no super-linear lower bound is known for the general problem, and no general linear-time algorithm has been found, so the precise complexity remains open.

status_evidence.title: Optimal Integer Alphabetic Trees in Linear Time
status_evidence.snippet: Optimal alphabetic binary trees can be constructed in O(n) time if the elements of the initial sequence are drawn from a domain that can be sorted in linear time.
status_evidence.claim: Linear-time algorithms are known only for restricted classes of inputs.

status_evidence.title: The Optimal Alphabetic Tree problem revisited
status_evidence.snippet: A modification of the Hu-Tucker algorithm runs in O(n) time for several classes of inputs that can be detected in linear time.
status_evidence.claim: Special cases admit O(n) algorithms; general complexity remains O(n log n) with only Ω(n) lower bound.

status_evidence.title: Some new results on constructing optimal alphabetic binary trees (UBC thesis)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies on constructing optimal alphabetic binary trees, with progress on special cases but the general gap between Ω(n) and O(n log n) remaining.
status_evidence.claim: The gap between the Ω(n) lower bound and the O(n log n) upper bound is unresolved.
